thread:
incident-bot: P1 alert — tenant Folkline (dedicated pool folkline-vpc-01) has sustained scheduler queue depth > 95th percentile for 12m, tail inference latency spiking. Noted customer SLA: enterprise VPC. https://console.redwood.example/d/folkline/queue

maya: I’m on it. seeing queue_depth around 470, max_batch_tokens spiking to 2048 and many small requests causing fragmentation.

sam: confirming — scheduler shows a lot of single-request batches, throughput is OK but tail latency > 2s for completion. Probably max_batch_tokens and coalescing thresholds need adjusting for this tenant.

maya: quick assessment — tenant pinned to rtx-a100-8, dedicated. traffic pattern changed (new feature rollout?). Do we have any recent deploys?

patrick: no infra deploys. Customer mentioned a canary last hour from their side. Ops says request token size increased by ~3x for certain endpoints.

maya: ok — mitigation plan options: 1) apply tenant shaper override to reduce scheduler.max_batch_tokens for folkline to force smaller token budgets per batch, 2) raise coalesce window slightly to allow more vanity coalescing, 3) temporarily route to a lower-capacity model variant to reduce per-token compute. Prefer 1+2 first.

sam: agree. can do a micro-adjust on scheduler knobs. I’ll apply a conservative change: set tenant override scheduler.max_batch_tokens=1024 and scheduler.coalesce_ms=8 (currently 3). That should reduce fragmentation without starving throughput.

maya: thumbs-up. Sam — please run the config update in staging-style first but we can target the tenant override directly since it's scoped. Include a dry-run logging flag.

sam: running now. command: 
```bash
infractl tenant patch folkline --pool folkline-vpc-01 --set 'shaper.scheduler.max_batch_tokens=1024' --set 'shaper.scheduler.coalesce_ms=8' --dry-run=false
```

console-bot: Patch accepted by control-plane. Rolling config to folkline-vpc-01 (2 hosts at a time). Patch id: patch-20250315-4521.

ops-bot: Applying change to node node-r11 and node-r12 now.

maya: monitoring Prometheus dashboards: watch queue_depth, avg_batch_size, tail_p95_latency, and model_token_throughput.

sam: here's immediate before/after snapshot (log snippet):
```json
{"ts":"2256789000","queue_depth":472,"avg_batch_size":1.2,"max_batch_tokens":2048,"p95_latency_ms":2150}
{"ts":"2256789200","queue_depth":210,"avg_batch_size":1.8,"max_batch_tokens":1024,"p95_latency_ms":780}
```

maya: nice — p95 dropped from ~2.15s to ~0.78s within the first rollout wave. queue depth halfing is promising.

patrick: customer impact: their dashboard shows error rates unchanged but response time improved for interactive endpoints. no dropped requests.

sam: still seeing a subset of long tails ~1.5s from very large token requests. For those we should consider a per-route cap or apply request-level token-shedding.

maya: agree — add a route override for /api/v2/generate-large to set max_request_tokens=1500 and fallback_model=redwood-small to avoid a single huge call blocking batches.

sam: applying second change: 
```bash
infractl tenant route patch folkline \
  --route "/api/v2/generate-large" \
  --set 'limits.max_request_tokens=1500' \
  --set 'routing.fallback_model=redwood-small-v2' \
  --dry-run=false
```

console-bot: Route patch accepted. Changes will be active within 30s.

maya: monitoring customer-facing latency. sending quick note to CS: "We applied targeted scheduler knobs and a route-level cap to reduce tail latency. We're watching and will follow up with a summary."

sam: raw CPU/GPU utilization on pool: GPUs at 72% avg, host CPU spikes transient. Not seeing OOMs.

maya: cool. let's let the changes bake for 15m. If metrics continue to improve, we keep these as default tenant overrides until next window.

lucas: (next-oncall) ping — I’ll take the 02:00–10:00 handoff. Any outstanding tasks for me?

maya: thanks lucas. action items for handoff:
- continue monitoring p95 and queue_depth (alert threshold lowered to p95>900ms for this tenant during mitigation)
- watch for any regressing error rates or capacity anomalies
- coordinate with Solutions for a follow-up with Folkline to assess if their canary change needs permanent shaper adjustments
- rollback plan: revert scheduler.max_batch_tokens to 2048 and coalesce_ms to 3 if we see throughput drop >10% or increased 5xxs

lucas: got it. I’ll keep the alerting escalated to the P1 rotation. Please paste the customer-facing note when you have it.

maya: posting customer note to #customer-success-desk and will add the config diffs: 
```text
We applied a targeted scheduler configuration to improve tail latency: reduced per-batch token budget for Folkline and increased coalesce window to allow better batching. We also added a per-route token cap and fallback model for very large requests. No request loss observed. Monitoring continues.
```

patrick: thumbs up from me. ETA for postmortem: collect 6h of metrics, then short blameless writeup.

incident-bot: P1 status: mitigated -> monitoring. Updated SLA impact: transient latency degradation for 12m, no SLA breach.

lucas: taking over. tagging @oncall-2 for visibility. leaving thread. :raised_hands:

maya: thanks all — closing live mitigation channel, will follow up with PM/SE sync and the postmortem link once ready. :white_check_mark:
